new_statements.quote: 5. Alama za mawimbi (toni): Kinyiha ni lugha ya toni, yaani, mawimbi ya maneno yanasaidia kutofautisha maana mbalimbali. Kwa mfano, tukiandika vhatelesile kwa Kinyiha, maana yake siyo wazi. Je, maana ni 'wamepika' au 'walipika'? Katika matamshi kuna tofauti ya mawimbi. Ikiwa na maana 'wamepika', wimbi la juu liko kwenye si, yaani, tunatamka vhateleSIle. Ikiwa na maana 'walipika', wimbi la juu liko kwenye vha, yaani, tunatamka VHAtelesile. Tunaonyesha tofauti hii katika maandishi kwa njia ya kuweka alama juu ya irabu inayobeba wimbi la juu katika vitenzi vya wakati uliopita. Kwa mfano: vhatelesile (wamepika), vhaatelesile (walipika jana/juzi), vhátelesile (walipika zamani); amanyile (amejua), aamanyile (alijua jana/juzi), ámanyile (alijua zamani).
new_statements.translation: 5. Pitch (tone) marks: Nyiha is a tone language, that is, the pitches of words help to distinguish different meanings. For example, if we write vhatelesile in Nyiha its meaning is not clear: is it 'they have cooked' or 'they cooked'? In pronunciation there is a difference of pitch. With the meaning 'they have cooked' the high pitch is on si, i.e. we say vhateleSIle. With the meaning 'they cooked (long ago)' the high pitch is on vha, i.e. we say VHAtelesile. We show this difference in writing by putting a mark over the vowel that carries the high pitch in past-tense verbs. E.g. vhatelesile 'they have cooked', vhaatelesile 'they cooked yesterday', vhátelesile 'they cooked long ago'; amanyile / aamanyile / ámanyile 'he has known / knew (recent) / knew (remote)'.

Shipupuusu kuvhaazya injango yiitu iya Shinyiha = Ni rahisi kusoma lugha yetu ya Kinyiha [It's Easy to Read our Nyiha Language]. Mbeya, Tanzania: SIL International. 4 pp. = SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 93698 (Subject Languages: Nyiha (Tanzania) [nih], Nyiha (Malawi) [nyr]; Content Language: [nih], [nyr]; Country: Malawi, Tanzania; 'Has Version': 1st Malawi ed. 2019 = entry 92263, A's work 1).
new_statements.locator: p.3, section '5. Alama za mawimbi (toni)' (the from extracted text drops the letters a and g of this font; the identical paragraph, fully lettered, is on p.16 of missed work 2, decoded)
new_statements.relation_note: Sec. 5 'Alama za mawimbi (toni)' states that Nyiha is a tone language in which pitch distinguishes meanings, illustrated with the verb vhatelesile: high pitch on -si- (vhateleSIle) = perfect 'they have cooked' vs high pitch on the subject prefix vha- (VHAtelesile) = remote past 'they cooked'; the orthography marks the high-toned vowel with an accent only on past-tense verbs (vhatelesile / vhaatelesile / vhátelesile; amanyile / aamanyile / ámanyile). Sec. 2 states long vowels are written double (aa ee ii oo uu). Nothing on stress/accent placement.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Lexical/grammatical tone: pitch contrasts distinguish verb tenses (H on penultimate -si- in the perfect vs H on the initial subject prefix in the remote past); tone written only where tense would otherwise be ambiguous. No word-stress rule given.
new_statements.exceptions: none; tone marking restricted to past-tense verbs
new_statements.identity_note: This is the Swahili-medium Tanzanian edition of the cross-border Shinyiha transition primer; the orthography and its explanatory notes were developed by SIL Mbeya with Mbozi (Tanzania) Nyiha speakers, i.e. the linguistic basis is Nyiha (Tanzania) nyih1240. SIL's own archive record for exactly this edition (93698, saved) lists Nyiha (Malawi) [nyr] as subject AND content language and Malawi as a country, and the 2019 Malawi edition (92263, 'language of instruction: Nyiha, aimed at Nyiha speakers in Malawi') is a version of it, so SIL applies this orthography -- tone marks included -- to the Kameme community. Our bibliography mentions entry 93698 only inside catalog-page notes ('literacy booklet, no further metadata'); the booklet itself was never a row and never opened because SIL marks it 'Not Available Online'. Whether the tone facts were re-checked with Kameme speakers is not stated anywhere; treat as a statement about the Mbozi-Malawi Nyiha standard, not fieldwork on Kameme speech. | Orthography and spelling-transition guide (Swahili -> Kinyiha) for Nyiha of Tanzania [nih] = nyih1240, produced in Mbeya with the Mbozi Nyiha team and SIL linguist Helen Eaton; no Malawi tagging seen for this title (no SIL archive record checked; fr.wikipedia cites it as langue nih). Listed because it carries the fully lettered version of the tone paragraph quoted under missed work 1 and adds vowel-length minimal pairs; it is the nearest open orthography statement for the Mbozi-Malawi Nyiha node.

sources.note: Describes MBOZI (Tanzania) Nyiha, glottocode nyih1240, not the Malawi variety: main accent on the stem syllable if it is long or the stem trisyllabic; with monosyllabic or short disyllabic stems the accent retracts to the preceding prefix syllable (even to the first prefix syllable); words of more than four syllables accent the penult. Noted here only because the Kameme stress marks in Lindfors et al. 2009 pattern the same way.
